mentions.name: Capability-based message-passing platform
mentions.description: A prototype software platform built around capabilities and message passing, targeting Linux and bare-metal RISC-V. It pursues a stackless design running on a flat address space with lightweight processes to minimize message-passing latency, and sandboxing so every process only accesses capabilities explicitly passed via messages. Work centers on a stackless scheduler, with a plan for preempting long-running or misbehaved tasks without per-process stacks or context-switch memory overhead. Planned next steps include layering Cap'n Proto or another high-performance serialization system to create a distributed, introspectable environment of object-capabilities exchanging typed messages — a hybrid of Smalltalk and the Erlang VM for building an entire operating system and user-space.
mentions.problem: Exploring what a post-UNIX paradigm of computing could look like.
